category: Instrument Control, Data Acquisition & Hardware Support
description: Serial, TCP/IP, UDP, VISA and Modbus instrument communication, data acquisition device configuration and streaming, and support packages for Arduino and Raspberry Pi hardware.

tools.name: serialport
tools.description: Open a connection to a serial (RS-232 / USB-serial) device, returning an object used for reading and writing. It replaces the legacy serial function with a simpler interface, automatic cleanup when the object is cleared, and byte- and terminator-based callbacks. Most bench instruments, microcontrollers and GPS modules use this interface.
tools.usage:
s = serialport(port, baudrate)
s = serialport(port, baudrate, Name, Value)
ports = serialportlist
configureTerminator(s, terminator)
configureCallback(s, 'terminator', @cb)
clear s

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port name such as 'COM3' on Windows or '/dev/ttyUSB0' on Linux.

parameters.name: 'Timeout'
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a read to complete (default 10).

tools.notes: Clearing the variable closes the port. Always flush before a new request to discard stale bytes.

tools.name: serialportlist
tools.description: List the serial ports present on the system, optionally restricted to those not already in use. It is the reliable way to discover which port a device enumerated on, rather than hard-coding a name. The result is a string array you can loop over.
tools.usage:
list = serialportlist
list = serialportlist("all")
list = serialportlist("available")

parameters.name: "all"
parameters.description: Every serial port known to the system (default).

parameters.name: "available"
parameters.description: Only ports that are not currently open.

tools.name: tcpclient
tools.description: Create a TCP/IP client connection to a server such as a networked instrument, a data service or another MATLAB session. Reading and writing use the same write, read, writeline and readline functions as serial ports. It replaces the legacy tcpip function and cleans up automatically when cleared.
tools.usage:
t = tcpclient(address, port)
t = tcpclient(address, port, Name, Value)
write(t, data)
data = read(t, count)
configureCallback(t, 'byte', n, @cb)

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Hostname or IP address of the server.

parameters.name: 'ConnectTimeout'
parameters.description: Seconds allowed to establish the connection.

parameters.name: 'EnableTransferDelay'
parameters.description: Logical; false disables Nagle's algorithm for lower latency.

tools.notes: Port 5025 is the conventional SCPI-over-TCP (raw socket) port for test instruments.

tools.name: tcpserver
tools.description: Create a TCP/IP server that listens for a client connection on a given port, so MATLAB can act as the server side of a link. Connection and data-available callbacks let you respond asynchronously without blocking. Use it to accept data from embedded devices, test rigs or other applications.
tools.usage:
server = tcpserver(port)
server = tcpserver(address, port)
server = tcpserver(___, Name, Value)
configureCallback(server, 'byte', n, @cb)
server.Connected

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Local interface to bind to; defaults to all interfaces.

parameters.name: 'ConnectionChangedFcn'
parameters.description: Callback invoked when a client connects or disconnects.

tools.name: udpport
tools.description: Create a UDP socket for connectionless datagram communication, supporting unicast, broadcast and multicast. UDP has no delivery guarantee but much lower latency and overhead than TCP, which suits telemetry and streaming sensor data. Each write and read handles a complete datagram.
tools.usage:
u = udpport
u = udpport(Name, Value)
write(u, data, destinationAddress, destinationPort)
data = read(u, count)
configureMulticast(u, address)

parameters.name: 'LocalPort'
parameters.description: Port to bind to for receiving.

parameters.name: 'EnableBroadcast'
parameters.description: Logical; allow sending to a broadcast address.

parameters.name: 'EnablePortSharing'
parameters.description: Logical; allow several sockets to bind to the same port.

parameters.name: 'Timeout' / 'ByteOrder'
parameters.description: Read timeout and numeric byte ordering.

tools.name: visadev
tools.description: Connect to a test and measurement instrument through a VISA resource string, covering USB-TMC, GPIB, TCP/IP-VXI11, serial and PXI interfaces uniformly. The same read/write functions work regardless of the physical bus, so instrument code is portable. It replaces the older visa function and interface-specific objects.
tools.usage:
v = visadev(resourceName)
list = visadevlist
writeline(v, command)
response = readline(v)
response = writeread(v, query)
data = readbinblock(v)

parameters.name: resourceName
parameters.description: VISA resource string or alias, e.g. 'USB0::0x0957::0x1799::MY12345::0::INSTR'.

parameters.name: 'EOIMode'
parameters.description: Logical; assert EOI at the end of a GPIB write.

tools.notes: Requires a vendor VISA implementation (NI-VISA, Keysight IO Libraries or similar) to be installed.

tools.name: visadevlist
tools.description: List every VISA resource currently visible to the installed VISA implementation, returning a table of resource names, aliases, vendors, models and serial numbers. It is how you discover the exact resource string to pass to visadev. Run it after connecting an instrument to confirm the driver sees it.
tools.usage:
list = visadevlist
list = visadevlist("Timeout", seconds)

parameters.name: "Timeout"
parameters.description: Seconds to spend scanning for devices.

tools.name: writeline
tools.description: Write a string to an interface object followed by the configured terminator, which is what almost every ASCII instrument protocol expects. It works identically for serialport, tcpclient, tcpserver, udpport and visadev objects. Configure the terminator first with configureTerminator.
tools.usage:
writeline(obj, data)
writeline(udpObj, data, destinationAddress, destinationPort)

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: A serialport, tcpclient, tcpserver, udpport or visadev object.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: String or character vector to send; the terminator is appended automatically.

tools.name: readline
tools.description: Read bytes from an interface object up to and including the configured terminator, returning the data as a string with the terminator stripped. It blocks until the terminator arrives or the timeout expires, returning a missing string on timeout. It is the standard way to read an ASCII instrument response.
tools.usage: data = readline(obj)

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: A serialport, tcpclient, tcpserver, udpport or visadev object with a configured terminator.

tools.notes: A missing string means the timeout expired before the terminator arrived; check with ismissing.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write raw binary or numeric data to an interface object, with an optional data type specifying how values are encoded on the wire. Use it for binary protocols, firmware uploads and waveform downloads where a terminator makes no sense. The object's ByteOrder property controls endianness.
tools.usage:
write(obj, data)
write(obj, data, datatype)
write(udpObj, data, datatype, address, port)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Numeric or char data to send.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a specified number of values of a given data type from an interface object. With no count it returns all bytes currently available in the input buffer without waiting. Use it for binary protocols and for draining a stream of sensor data.
tools.usage:
data = read(obj)
data = read(obj, count)
data = read(obj, count, datatype)

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of values to read; blocks until they arrive or the timeout expires.

tools.name: writeread
tools.description: Send a command to a VISA instrument and read its terminated response in a single call, which is the natural pattern for SCPI queries. It handles the write, the wait and the read together and avoids the common bug of forgetting to read a response. Use it for every query that returns ASCII.
tools.usage: response = writeread(visaObj, command)

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: SCPI query string, normally ending in a question mark.

tools.name: configureTerminator
tools.description: Set the line terminator used by readline and writeline on an interface object, optionally different for reading and writing. Getting this wrong is the single most common cause of instrument timeouts. Consult the instrument manual for whether it expects LF, CR or CR/LF.
tools.usage:
configureTerminator(obj, terminator)
configureTerminator(obj, readTerminator, writeTerminator)

parameters.name: terminator
parameters.description: "LF", "CR", "CR/LF", "LF/CR", or an integer ASCII code from 0 to 255.

tools.name: modbus
tools.description: Communicate with PLCs and industrial devices over Modbus TCP or Modbus RTU (serial). It exposes the standard register model through read and write calls that take a target type such as 'holdingregs' or 'coils'. Common in factory automation, building control and energy monitoring.
tools.usage:
m = modbus('tcpip', deviceAddress, port)
m = modbus('serialrtu', port, Name, Value)
data = read(m, target, address, count, serverId)
write(m, target, address, values, serverId)
writeRead(m, ___)

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of registers or coils to read.

tools.name: daq
tools.description: Create a DataAcquisition object for a specified vendor, which is the container to which you add analog, digital and counter channels. It supports single-point reads, finite and continuous clocked acquisition, and simultaneous generation. This is the modern session-based interface for Data Acquisition Toolbox.
tools.usage:
dq = daq(vendor)
ch = addinput(dq, deviceID, channelID, measurementType)
dq.Rate = rate;
data = read(dq, duration)
start(dq, 'Continuous')
stop(dq)

parameters.name: 'Rate'
parameters.description: Scan rate in samples per second per channel.

parameters.name: 'ScansAvailableFcn'
parameters.description: Callback invoked when new scans are ready during continuous acquisition.

parameters.name: 'ScansAvailableFcnCount'
parameters.description: Number of scans that triggers the callback.

tools.notes: Requires the vendor's hardware support package. daqlist shows which devices are visible.

tools.name: daqlist
tools.description: List the data acquisition devices available on the system, returning a table of device IDs, models, vendors and detailed channel information. Use it to discover the device ID and valid channel names before configuring a DataAcquisition object. The DeviceInfo column expands to show subsystem capabilities and supported ranges.
tools.usage:
d = daqlist
d = daqlist(vendor)

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to one vendor: 'ni', 'adi', 'mcc', 'digilent', 'directsound'.

tools.name: addinput
tools.description: Add an input channel to a DataAcquisition object, specifying the device, channel and measurement type. The returned channel object exposes properties such as range, terminal configuration and coupling that you set for correct scaling. Every channel you add is sampled on the same clock at the object's Rate.
tools.usage:
ch = addinput(dq, deviceID, channelID, measurementType)
[ch, idx] = addinput(___)

parameters.name: channelID
parameters.description: Channel name such as "ai0", or a vector of them.

tools.name: addoutput
tools.description: Add an output channel to a DataAcquisition object for generating analog voltage, current or digital signals. Output channels are clocked together with input channels, which allows synchronized stimulus-response measurements. Load the waveform with preload or write and then start the generation.
tools.usage:
ch = addoutput(dq, deviceID, channelID, measurementType)
[ch, idx] = addoutput(___)

tools.name: readwrite
tools.description: Perform a synchronized finite acquisition and generation in one call: output the supplied waveform while simultaneously recording the input channels. Because both share the same hardware clock, input and output samples are exactly aligned. It is the standard way to measure a frequency response or a device transfer characteristic.
tools.usage:
scanData = readwrite(dq, outputSignal)
scanData = readwrite(dq, outputSignal, "OutputFormat", fmt)

parameters.name: outputSignal
parameters.description: Matrix with one column per output channel, defining the generated waveform.

tools.name: start
tools.description: Begin a background acquisition or generation on a DataAcquisition object, returning immediately so MATLAB stays responsive. In 'Continuous' mode data flows until you call stop, delivered through the ScansAvailableFcn callback. Use it for long recordings, live displays and closed-loop control.
tools.usage:
start(dq)
start(dq, "Continuous")
start(dq, "Duration", duration)
start(dq, "NumScans", n)
start(dq, "RepeatOutput")

parameters.name: "Continuous"
parameters.description: Acquire or generate until stop is called.

parameters.name: "Duration" / "NumScans"
parameters.description: Finite acquisition length in time or scans.

parameters.name: "RepeatOutput"
parameters.description: Loop the preloaded output waveform indefinitely.

tools.name: stop
tools.description: Stop a background acquisition or generation started with start, halting the hardware and any pending callbacks. Data already in the buffer can still be read afterwards, and flush discards it. Always stop before reconfiguring channels or clearing the object.
tools.usage: stop(dq)

tools.name: arduino
tools.description: Connect to an Arduino board over USB, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi and control it interactively from MATLAB without writing any sketch code. The returned object exposes digital and analog I/O, PWM, servo, I2C and SPI through method calls. Requires the MATLAB Support Package for Arduino Hardware.
tools.usage:
a = arduino
a = arduino(port, board)
a = arduino(port, board, Name, Value)
configurePin(a, pin, mode)
clear a

parameters.name: 'ForceBuildOn'
parameters.description: Logical; rebuild and reflash the server sketch.

tools.name: readVoltage
tools.description: Read the voltage on an Arduino analog input pin, returned in volts after the board's ADC scaling is applied. It is the simplest way to acquire sensor data from potentiometers, thermistors, light sensors and analog outputs. Each call performs one conversion, so loop with a pause for time series data.
tools.usage: voltage = readVoltage(a, pin)
tools.notes: Each read costs a USB round trip, so the achievable sample rate is only tens of hertz.

tools.name: writeDigitalPin
tools.description: Set an Arduino digital pin high or low, configuring it as an output automatically if needed. Use it to drive LEDs, relays, motor-driver enable lines and other on/off actuators. For proportional control use writePWMVoltage or writePWMDutyCycle instead.
tools.usage: writeDigitalPin(a, pin, value)

tools.name: raspi
tools.description: Connect to a Raspberry Pi over the network and control its GPIO, I2C, SPI, serial and camera peripherals from MATLAB. It also provides shell command execution and file transfer to and from the board. Requires the MATLAB Support Package for Raspberry Pi Hardware.
tools.usage:
rpi = raspi
rpi = raspi(deviceAddress, username, password)
writeDigitalPin(rpi, pin, value)
value = readDigitalPin(rpi, pin)
system(rpi, command)
getFile(rpi, remoteFile, localFolder)

parameters.name: deviceAddress
parameters.description: Hostname or IP address of the Pi.
